# Gallium

> Gallium is a standalone local web task engine for AI agents. Submit a goal through MCP or the CLI. Gallium chooses a route, adapts to observed page state, and returns source evidence or a verified result from a configured workflow.

## Start here

- [Examples](https://davidjbeveridge.github.io/gallium/#workflow): Public HTTPS retrieval, live page exploration, and a verified local fixture change.
- [Engine architecture](https://davidjbeveridge.github.io/gallium/#engine): Route selection, live feedback, durable state, concurrency, and human handoff.
- [Quickstart](https://davidjbeveridge.github.io/gallium/#install): Run the fixture demo or install the engine with Git and Node.js 24 or later.
- [Setup and configuration](https://github.com/davidjbeveridge/gallium/blob/main/docs/guide.md): Configure the CLI, stdio MCP server, Chrome bridge, model router, and procedures.
- [Validation](https://github.com/davidjbeveridge/gallium/blob/main/VALIDATION.md): Test commands, observed outcomes, and qualification boundaries.

## How the engine works

- Public goals use a configured Jev router through OpenRouter System One. Gallium tries direct HTTPS for document lookups and can move to bounded, same-origin browser exploration. Explicit UI goals start in the live page. The result includes a source URL, passage, and evidence hash. The model assesses relevance.
- Configured goals match existing procedures. Code prefers direct HTTP, then browser-session requests, then browser interaction among eligible web procedures. Signed-in workflows and mutations require a configured account, allowed actions, and an independent result check. The browser routes use installed desktop Chrome through the bridge.
- Live observations inform the next step during a run. The SQLite journal tracks operation identity, configured route choices, effects, and human control across restarts. The current release uses fixed route preference. Learned route ranking is a research direction.
